threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'excuse me' when passing folks on the path. Everyone else just power walks through like they own the pavement.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and a guy was singing opera to the driver. Not a soul batted an eye—classic South London moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the guy at the corner Kiez cafe remembers your order but you still can’t recall his name. That’s when you know you’re home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM and hear a techno beat pulsing from the kebab shop while bike messengers zip past.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they react to BART delays; the ones who shrug and carry on know the struggle, while the newcomers stress out over the inevitable.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full dive gear board the 14 Mission today. He just stood there, fins on, totally unfazed by the stares. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all we eat is paella and tapas, but a proper Gracià breakfast is a xuixo and café amb llet from the corner bakery.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell the newcomers by their puzzled looks when the tram screeches to a halt unexpectedly; locals just roll their eyes and keep scrolling on their phones.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look up at the signs when the tube's delayed—locals just roll their eyes and carry on with a coffee in hand.
Caught a guy on the 36 last night passionately reciting Shakespeare to his mate. A proper performance for the late-night crowd, totally unexpected.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street artist spray-painting a mural of a cat on a crumbling wall while a toddler danced nearby. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's not uncommon to see a whole café morph into an art gallery overnight, complete with jazz musicians making an impromptu appearance.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their knack for dodging pigeon poop on Valencia while still sipping on a pour-over from Ritual.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the N-Judah stuck behind a street performer juggling on the tracks during rush hour. Nothing says SF like a jammed train and a clown.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists crowd the Fontana metro but miss the quiet cafes on Gran de Gràcia, where locals sip vermut and the world feels far away.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot a newcomer by their bewilderment at the bus schedules; the locals just nod and know when to jump on.
